lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Thank you for watching our play! Today, we walk down the mountain path from the theater. It's a long walk. Look! There's white steam everywhere. This is the Village of Springs. An old capybara comes to meet us. Her name is Granny Capy. She smiles and says, Welcome to the Village of Springs! Kiko puts her hand in a little spring. Oh, it's warm! The spring water here is warm. Say it with me. The spring water here is warm. Wonderful! Let's read the sign by the stone path. "Welcome to the Village of Springs! There are twelve warm springs in our village. The biggest one is the Heart Spring. It is in the middle of the village. You can put your hands and feet in the water. Please do not swim in the springs. Warm water, warm hearts! From the Spring Inn." How many springs are there? Twelve. What is the biggest spring? The Heart Spring. Now, phonics. Today, c h says k. Echo. Hello, hello, hello. School. A short k sound. Chorus. Let's sing together. Character. Birimo is a funny character. Let's go and find the Heart Spring!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, The spring water here is warm. Today is our first morning at the Spring Inn. Haru, Riko and Birimo are ready to explore. But Kiko is very quiet. She is holding her head. Riko asks her, What's wrong? Kiko says, I have a headache. I'm tired. The mountain path was very long. Say it with me. What's wrong? Good! When a friend looks sick or sad, you can ask, What's wrong? Granny Capy gives Kiko a cup of warm herbal tea. Then she shows us a small card in our room. Let's read it. "Feeling tired after a long trip? Here are three tips. One, drink some water or warm tea. Two, sit down in a quiet place and close your eyes. Three, go to bed early tonight. If you feel sick, please tell a grown-up. You will feel better tomorrow. Rest well! Granny Capy." What can you drink? Water or warm tea. When should you go to bed? Early tonight. Now, phonics. Today, a c h e says ache. Headache. My head hurts. Toothache. My tooth hurts. Earache. My ear hurts. Ache. The e at the end is silent. Rest well, Kiko!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, What's wrong? Kiko had a good rest, and now she feels better. Tonight, there is a small fair in the village. There are food stalls with rice balls, soup and cakes. Birimo is so happy. He eats and eats. Later, he sits down on a bench and holds his tummy. Haru asks, Are you OK? Birimo says, Not really. My stomach hurts. I ate too much. Say it with me. My stomach hurts. I ate too much. Great! Ms. Emma tells Birimo to sit and rest. Let's read the menu at the soup stall. "Village Fair Food Stalls. Open tonight from five to eight. Rice balls: salmon or plum. Hot vegetable soup. Sweet potato cakes. Fresh fruit cups. Our tip: eat slowly and stop when you feel full. Your stomach will thank you! Water is free at every stall. Please put your trash in the bins." What kind of soup is there? Hot vegetable soup. When should you stop eating? When you feel full. Now, phonics. Stomach. The c h says k. Stomachache. Stomach plus ache. Bellyache. Belly is another word for stomach. Orchestra. Here, c h says k, too. Eat slowly, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, My stomach hurts. I ate too much. This morning, Haru doesn't feel well. His face is red, and he feels hot. He has a fever（ねつ）. Haru has had a fever since yesterday. Ms. Emma takes him to the little clinic. The village doctor is a kind deer named Dr. Fern. Dr. Fern asks, How long have you had a fever? Haru says, Since yesterday. I have a cough and a sore throat. Say it with me. How long have you had a fever? Since yesterday. Very good! Dr. Fern checks Haru carefully and writes a note. Let's read it. "Dr. Fern's Note for Haru. You have a small cold. Don't worry. Drink lots of water. Rest in bed today and tomorrow. Sleep well at night. Cough into your elbow. Tell Ms. Emma if you feel worse. Then come back and see me. Get lots of rest!" How many days should Haru rest in bed? Two days, today and tomorrow. What should he drink? Lots of water. Now, phonics. Backache. Back plus ache. Mechanic. The c h says k. Anchor. A big ship has an anchor. Christmas. Again, c h says k. Rest well, Haru!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, How long have you had a fever? Since yesterday. Haru is resting in his room at the Spring Inn today. He can't come out and play. So, let's make him a get-well card! Riko draws a big sun. Kiko draws some flowers. Birimo draws a rice ball, of course. Then, we write a message. I hope you feel better soon. Say it with me. I hope you feel better soon. Lovely! We can also write, Get well soon! And, Take care of yourself. Let's read our card together. "Dear Haru, We miss you! The village is quiet without you. Please drink lots of water and get lots of sleep. Granny Capy is making you warm soup. Birimo wants to play cards with you. Get well soon! Take care of yourself. I hope you feel better soon. Love, Riko, Kiko, Birimo and Ms. Emma" Who is making soup? Granny Capy. What does Birimo want to do? Play cards with Haru. Now, phonics. Let's review. School. C h says k. Stomach. C h says k again. Headache. A c h e says ache. Stomachache. Stomach plus ache. Let's take the card to Haru!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I hope you feel better soon. Good news! Haru feels much better today. Early in the morning, we hear music in the village square. A young snow monkey is jumping and stretching. His name is Toto. He waves and says, Come and join us! Toto does morning exercises with the village kids. Haru asks him, How often do you exercise? Toto says, Every day! I stretch every morning. Say it with me. How often do you exercise? Super! You can answer, Three times a week. Or, Every day. Let's read the poster in the square. "Morning Exercise in the Village Square! Every day at seven o'clock. Ten minutes of stretching, then ten minutes of walking. Everyone is welcome, young and old. Wear comfortable shoes. Bring some water. Toto will lead the exercises today. Move your body and start your day with a smile!" What time does it start? At seven o'clock. What should you bring? Some water. Now, phonics. Today, some letters are silent. Knee. Don't say the k. Wrist. Don't say the w. Thumb. Don't say the b. Muscle. Don't say the c. Let's stretch together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Eating breakfast is good for your brain. Today, it's raining in the village. We stay inside the Spring Inn. Toto comes to visit with his tablet. He loves games and videos. Ms. Emma asks, How much screen time do you have? Haru says, I play video games for one hour a day. Toto says, After one hour, I take a break and go outside. Say it with me. I play video games for one hour a day. Good job! Games and videos are fun. The important thing is a good balance. Let's read a column in the Spring News. "Screen Time Tips. Games and videos can be fun and useful. Here are some tips for a good balance. Talk with your family about a time limit. Rest your eyes every thirty minutes. Look far away for a moment. Turn off screens one hour before bed. Then go outside, play and move your body!" When should you turn off screens? One hour before bed. How often should you rest your eyes? Every thirty minutes. Now, phonics. Talk. Don't say the l. Palm. Don't say the l. Honest. Don't say the h. An honest answer. Calf. The l is silent. Let's find a good balance!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I play video games for one hour a day. The village will have a Health Festival soon. Granny Capy asks us to help. So, we did a habit survey. We asked eight people in the village about their habits. Today, we present the results. Riko says, Five people eat breakfast every day. Say it with me. Five people eat breakfast every day. Great! Kiko says, Most people sleep for nine hours or more. Haru says, Only two people exercise every day. Let's read our survey chart together. "Habit Survey for the Health Festival. We asked eight people. Eat breakfast every day: five people. Sleep for nine hours or more: six people. Exercise every day: two people. Wash hands before meals: seven people. Favorite healthy snack: fruit! Most people want to walk more. Thank you for answering our survey!" How many people did we ask? Eight. How many people wash their hands before meals? Seven. Now, phonics. Let's review. Knee. Silent k. Should. Silent l. Hour. Silent h. Toothache. Tooth plus ache. You are great survey reporters!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Five people eat breakfast every day. Our survey is ready for the Health Festival. Tonight, we sit by the fire at the Spring Inn. Granny Capy gives us warm herbal tea. Haru asks, How long have you lived here? Granny Capy smiles and says, I've lived here for ten years. Before that, I lived by the sea. Say it with me. I've lived here for ten years. Wonderful! I've lived here means she came here long ago, and she still lives here now. For ten years tells us how long. There's an old photo on the wall. Under the photo, there's a little note. Let's read it together. "The Spring Inn. Ten years ago, Granny Capy came here from the seaside. The old inn was empty, and the garden was full of weeds. She cleaned every room and planted herbs in the garden. Now travelers come from far away. They rest in the warm springs and drink her herbal tea." Where did Granny Capy live before? By the sea. What did she plant in the garden? Herbs. Now, phonics. For ten years. For is short and soft. Ten years is strong. For many years. For a long time. Long is strong. For six months. Say them like a song. Good night, everyone. Sweet dreams at the Spring Inn!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I've lived here for ten years. Granny Capy came to the village ten years ago. Today, it's raining, so we stay inside the Spring Inn. There's an old piano in the lobby. Riko sits down and plays a gentle song. Granny Capy claps her paws. Riko says, I've played the piano since I was five. Say it with me. I've played the piano since I was five. Beautiful! Since tells us the starting point. Riko started at five, and she still plays today. Haru says, I've done karate since I was seven. Kiko loves drawing, and Birimo loves cooking. Granny Capy puts a poster on the lobby wall. Let's read it. "Rainy Day Show at the Spring Inn! This evening, our guests will share their favorite things. Riko will play the piano. Haru will show some karate moves. Kiko will draw pictures of the springs. Birimo will cook sweet potato soup for everyone. Come to the lobby at six o'clock. Everyone is welcome!" What will Kiko do? She will draw pictures of the springs. What time does the show start? At six o'clock. Now, phonics. Since I was five. Since is short. Five is strong. Since April. Since kindergarten. Kin, der, gar, ten. Since Monday. Monday is strong. What have you done for a long time? Tell a friend!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I've played the piano since I was five. Today, we sit by the foot spring in the village square. We put our feet in the warm water. Ahh, so nice! Toto, the young snow monkey, sits next to us. He watches Haru and Riko. They laugh and joke all the time. Toto asks Haru, How long have you known Riko? Say it with me. How long have you known Riko? Great! Haru says, I've known her since kindergarten. We've been friends for five years. Then Toto shows us a page in the Spring News. Let's read it together. "Old Friends. Granny Capy and Dr. Fern have been friends for ten years. They met on Granny Capy's first day in the village. Dr. Fern helped her with her heavy bags. Now they drink herbal tea together every Sunday. Granny Capy says, A good friend is like a warm spring. You feel better with them." How long have they been friends? For ten years. When do they drink tea together? Every Sunday. Now, phonics. For three days. For is how long. Since last week. Since is when it started. For two hours. Two hours is strong. Since this morning. Morning is strong. Who is your good friend? Give them a big smile today!

Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. We've stayed at the Spring Inn for five days! And Haru has felt much better since Wednesday. Granny Capy gives us the guest book. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I've practiced karate for three years. Today, we walk up the mountain path above the village. The sun is hot, and there are no clouds. Kiko stops and says, I'm so thirsty. Ms. Emma gives her a water bottle and says, You should drink more water. Say it with me. You should drink more water. Great! We use should for good advice. Birimo's face is red. Haru says, It's hot today. You should wear a hat. At the side of the path, there's a wooden sign. Let's read it together. "Sunny Hill Path. Walking time: about one hour. Before you go, wear a hat and comfortable shoes. Bring a water bottle. The spring water at the top is drinkable, so you can fill your bottle there. Feeling tired? Take a short rest under the big tree. Please take your trash home." What should you wear? A hat and comfortable shoes. Where can you fill your bottle? At the top. Now, phonics. Comfortable. Say it short, comf, ta, ble. Drinkable. You can drink it. Washable. You can wash it. Valuable. Value, then able. Very important. Water is valuable on a hot day. Keep drinking, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, You should drink more water. This morning, we meet Toto in the square for morning exercises. But Haru can't jump, and he can't keep up. He says, I'm hungry and sleepy. Riko asks, Did you eat breakfast? No, he didn't. He got up late, so he skipped it. Kiko says, You shouldn't skip breakfast. Say it with me. You shouldn't skip breakfast. Good! Should not, shouldn't. It's gentle advice. Haru read comics until midnight. So Ms. Emma says, You shouldn't stay up late. Dr. Fern has a poster on the clinic door. Let's read it together. "Dr. Fern's Morning Tips. Breakfast gives your body and brain energy for the day. Without breakfast, you can feel hungry, sleepy and grumpy. Try rice, eggs, fruit or a glass of milk. No time? Eat a banana and a piece of toast. And go to bed early, so you can wake up on time." What can you eat with no time? A banana and a piece of toast. How can you wake up on time? Go to bed early. Now, phonics. Enjoyable. Enjoy, able. Readable. Easy to read. Believable. Believe, drop the e, able. Reliable. Rely, change y to i, able. Breakfast first, then fun!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, You shouldn't skip breakfast. Today, Haru eats a big breakfast. He feels great! But where is Riko? She's in the study room at the Spring Inn. She wants to learn every health word for the festival quiz. Kiko looks at the clock. Riko, you've studied for three hours! Riko rubs her eyes. Haru says, Why don't you take a break? Say it with me. Why don't you take a break? Nice and kind! This is a soft way to give advice. Then Birimo says, Why don't we go for a walk? Riko smiles. That's a good idea. On the study room door, there's a note from Granny Capy. Let's read it together. "Study Room Rules. One, open the window for fresh air. Two, drink some water. Three, after thirty minutes, stand up and stretch. Four, after one hour, take a ten-minute break and go outside. Your brain needs rest, too. Five, get a good sleep every night. Six, be kind to yourself." What should you do after one hour? Take a ten-minute break. What does your brain need? Rest. Now, phonics. Foldable. You can fold it. Bendable. You can bend it. Breakable. Be careful! Adorable. Adore, drop the e, able. So cute! Now, close your books. Let's go outside!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Why don't you take a break? Riko took a break, and now she feels fresh. Today, there's big news. The Spring News has a new advice corner. Its name is Ask Birimo! Birimo is so excited. The first letter is here. It begins, Dear Birimo, I can't sleep well. What should I do? Say it with me. Dear Birimo, I can't sleep well. What should I do? Well done! What should I do? asks for advice. Let's read the whole letter together. "Dear Birimo, I can't sleep well. What should I do? I go to bed at nine, but I'm still awake at eleven. I play games on my tablet in bed. In the morning, I'm always sleepy at school. My friends say I yawn all day. Please help me! From Sleepy Squirrel" When does Sleepy Squirrel go to bed? At nine. What does Sleepy Squirrel do in bed? Plays games on a tablet. So, what's your advice? You should read a book before bed. Don't look at screens before bed. Now, phonics. Fixable. You can fix it. This problem is fixable! Changeable. Keep the e. Noticeable. Keep the e. Unforgettable. Double t. You can't forget it. Sleep well tonight, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Dear Birimo, I can't sleep well. What should I do? Today is a very special day. This is our 800th lesson! 800 lessons! Thank you for learning with us every day. You are amazing! To celebrate, we have an Advice Show on the village stage. Villagers ask, What should I do? We give advice with a reason. Toto says, I always feel sleepy in class. Haru answers, I think you should go to bed early because sleep is important. Say it with me. I think you should go to bed early because sleep is important. Fantastic! Because gives the reason. Toto says, That's good advice. Thank you! Let's read the poster for the show. "800 Lessons Party and Advice Show! Today is our 800th English lesson. Come to the village stage at three o'clock. Bring your problems, big or small. Birimo and his friends will give you advice. After the show, there will be herbal tea and a big 800 cake for everyone. Everyone is welcome. Please come!" What time does the show start? At three o'clock. What will there be after the show? Herbal tea and a big cake. Now, phonics. Comfortable. Since Monday. Since is short. Listen. Don't say the t. Headache. Head, ache. Happy 800 lessons, everyone! Let's keep going together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I think you should go to bed early because sleep is important. What a great advice show! Today, Kiko is very quiet. She is sitting by the window at the Spring Inn. Next week, she has to give a speech at the Health Festival. She says, I'm worried about the festival speech. Riko asks her, What do you do when you're worried? Kiko thinks for a moment. Then she says, When I'm worried, I talk to my mom. Say it with me. When I'm worried, I talk to my mom. Wonderful! Talking really helps. Granny Capy has a poster on the wall of the inn. Let's read it together. "Feeling Worried? Everyone feels worried sometimes. It is a normal feeling. Here are three ideas. One: Talk to your family, a teacher or a good friend. Two: Take a slow walk or drink some warm tea. Three: Write your worries on paper. Then fold the paper and put it away. Small steps help a lot. Warm water, warm hearts!" Is it OK to feel worried? Yes, it is. What can you write on paper? Your worries. Now, phonics. Week. There are seven days in a week. Weak. Not strong. They sound the same! Here. Come here. Hear. Listen with your ear. There's an ear in hear! Kiko, we are here for you.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, When I'm worried, I talk to my mom. Today, we are sitting by the Heart Spring. The water is warm, and the steam is soft and white. Kiko practiced her speech this morning, and her heart was beating fast. So Ms. Emma teaches everyone a calm-down trick. Take a deep breath. Count to five. Say it with me. Take a deep breath. Count to five. Very good! Now breathe（いきを する）with me. Breathe in through your nose. One, two, three, four, five. Breathe out slowly. Kiko smiles and says, I feel calm now. There is a little wooden sign by the spring. Let's read it. "Heart Spring Calm Corner. Sit down on the warm stones and close your eyes. Breathe in through your nose and count to five. Then breathe out slowly through your mouth. Do this three times. Listen to the sound of the water. Feel the warm steam on your face. Now you are ready for a calm and happy day." How many times do you do it? Three times. How do you breathe in? Through your nose. Now, phonics. Piece. A piece of cake. Peace. Quiet and calm. Nose. Touch your nose. Knows. Birimo knows the answer. The k is silent! Peace and quiet, everyone.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Take a deep breath. Count to five. Today, Toto is not at morning exercise. Riko finds him alone on a bench in the village square. Toto looks sad. His best friend Mimi moved away to another village. Toto misses her very much. Haru sits next to him and says, It's OK to feel sad sometimes. Say it with me. It's OK to feel sad sometimes. Beautiful! Every feeling is OK. Then Kiko has an idea. You can write her a letter! Granny Capy brings a copy of The Spring News. Let's read the Feelings Corner. "Sad days come to everyone. Kids feel sad, and grown-ups feel sad, too. That is OK. When you feel sad, tell a grown-up in your family or a teacher. You can also draw a picture, hug a pet or look at the clouds. Sad feelings often get smaller when you share them. Tomorrow can be a brighter day." Do grown-ups feel sad, too? Yes, they do. Who can you tell? A grown-up in your family or a teacher. Now, phonics. Flour. We make bread with flour. Flower. A pretty flower for Mimi. Whole. The whole cake. The w is silent. Hole. A hole in the ground. Same sound, different words! Toto, we are with you.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, You did your best. I'm proud of you. Today, everyone makes a calm-down plan for the Health Festival. We will put our plans in the calm-down corner. Haru goes first. He says, When I'm angry, I count to ten. Say it with me. When I'm angry, I count to ten. Excellent! Riko says, When I'm sad, I hug my teddy bear. Kiko says, When I'm nervous, I take deep breaths. Now let's read Birimo's plan. He drew a lot of food on it! "My Calm-Down Plan by Birimo. When I'm angry, I count to ten. Then I drink some water. When I'm sad, I hug my teddy bear, Mr. Fluff. When I'm nervous, I take deep breaths. When I feel weak and hungry, I eat a healthy snack. Feelings come and go, like the steam over the spring. Every feeling is OK." What is his teddy bear's name? Mr. Fluff. What does he do when he's angry? He counts to ten. Now, phonics. Weak. Not strong. It sounds like week. Enjoyable. Enjoy plus able. For a long time. The word for is short and soft. Walk. The l is silent. Great plans, everyone. Let's enjoy a calm, happy week!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, When I'm angry, I count to ten. Today, we are at the Spring Inn. Granny Capy gives everyone a big piece of paper. Our trip will end soon. So let's make a healthy week plan for home. Haru writes first. He says, On Monday, I'm going to walk to school. Say it with me. On Monday, I'm going to walk to school. Super! Riko says, On Wednesday, I'm going to eat more vegetables. Kiko says, On Saturday, I'm going to play outside. Now let's read Haru's plan. "Haru's Healthy Week Plan. Monday: walk to school with my friends. Tuesday: go to bed at nine. Wednesday: eat more vegetables. Thursday: drink water, not sweet drinks. Friday: stretch my arms and wrists for ten minutes. Saturday: play outside with my friends. Sunday: help cook a healthy dinner with Dad. Every day: wash my hands and smile!" What is Haru going to do on Tuesday? Go to bed at nine. Who is he going to cook with? His dad. Now, phonics. Stomach. The ch sounds like k. Wrist. The w is silent. Since yesterday. Since tells us the starting time. Washable. You can wash it. Hear. Listen. It sounds like here. What a healthy week!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, On Monday, I'm going to walk to school. Today, we are getting ready for the health quiz. The festival is in two days! Riko is the quiz host. She holds a small bell. Her first question is, How many hours should children sleep? Say it with me. How many hours should children sleep? Great! Haru rings the bell and answers, Nine to twelve hours. Correct! Then Riko asks, Is it true or false? Kiko shouts, It's true! Dr. Fern wrote the quiz cards. Let's read one card together. "Health Festival Quiz. Question one: How many hours should children sleep? A: five to six hours. B: nine to twelve hours. Question two: True or false? Washing your hands helps stop germs. Question three: True or false? When you feel sick, you should tell an adult. Good luck, everyone!" What is the answer to question one? B, nine to twelve hours. Is question three true or false? It's true! Now, phonics. Earache. Ear plus ache. Ouch! Hour. The h is silent. We say an hour. For two hours. Say for softly. Readable. Easy to read. Peace. It sounds like piece. Quiz masters, you are ready!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, How many hours should children sleep? Today, Kiko gets a letter from her pen friend back home. Her pen friend feels sleepy and grumpy every morning. Kiko wants to help. She walks with Toto every morning here, and she feels great. So she writes a letter of advice. She starts with, Dear friend, you should try a morning walk. Say it with me. Dear friend, you should try a morning walk. Perfect! Let's read Kiko's letter. "Dear friend, How are you? You feel sleepy every morning. You should try a morning walk. It's good for your body and your mind. Walk for ten minutes before breakfast. Look at the sky and listen to the birds. Then eat a good breakfast. I walk with Toto every morning here. I feel great! Your friend, Kiko" How long should her friend walk? For ten minutes. What should her friend eat after the walk? A good breakfast. Now, phonics. Character. The ch sounds like k. Salmon. The l is silent. Since April. Since tells us the starting time. Valuable. Very important. Drop the e and add able. Write. Write a letter. The w is silent. Your letters are valuable gifts!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Dear friend, you should try a morning walk. Today is our goodbye walk around the Village of Springs. We walk along the stone path, past the clinic and the Spring Inn. Haru smiles and says, We've been here for two weeks, and I feel great! Say it with me. We've been here for two weeks, and I feel great! Wonderful! Birimo sits down on a rock. Riko asks, What's wrong? Birimo says, I'm a little tired. Kiko says, You should rest. Then, look! There's a rainbow over the Heart Spring! It shines in the warm steam. Granny Capy smiles and says, Follow the rainbow. It is a bridge to faraway friends. Maybe it leads to the Rainbow Bridge! Here is today's Spring News. "Thank You, Visitors! Our friends from far away came two weeks ago. They helped with the habit survey, the advice show and the health quiz. Haru had a fever, but now he is strong. Kiko was worried, but now she is brave. Tomorrow is the Health Festival. Come to the village square at ten!" What time is the festival? At ten. Was Haru sick? Yes, but now he is strong. Now, phonics. Backache. Back plus ache. Climb. The b is silent. For a week. Say for softly. Reliable. You can count on it. Flower. A spring flower. What a beautiful rainbow!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, We've been here for two weeks, and I feel great! Today is the Health Festival in the village square. Everyone is here. Granny Capy, Dr. Fern and Toto are in the front row. First, Toto leads the morning exercise. Then, Kiko gives her speech. She takes a deep breath, and she does it! At the end, everyone shouts, Healthy body, happy mind! Say it with me. Healthy body, happy mind! Fantastic! Let's read the festival program. "Village of Springs Health Festival. At ten, morning exercise with Toto. At half past ten, habit survey results. At eleven, Kiko's speech. At half past eleven, health quiz with prizes. At twelve, healthy lunch at the Spring Inn. All day, the calm-down corner is open by the Heart Spring. Warm water, warm hearts!" What time is Kiko's speech? At eleven. Where is the lunch? At the Spring Inn. After the festival, we say, Thank you for everything, Granny Capy! Then the rainbow appears again over the Heart Spring. Let's follow the rainbow to the Rainbow Bridge! Now, phonics. Echo. The ch sounds like k. Headache. Head plus ache. Knee. The k is silent. Since kindergarten. Since tells us the start. Unforgettable. We will never forget it. Week. Seven days. What an unforgettable stay!
